facts.statement: Mycterosuchus was an extinct genus of teleosaurid crocodyliform that lived in England during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Mycterosuchus is an extinct genus of teleosaurid crocodyliform from the Middle Jurassic (Callovian) of England.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analysis suggests Mycterosuchus is distantly related to the type species of Steneosaurus, despite earlier synonymization.
facts.quote: Although previously synonymized with Steneosaurus, recent cladistic analysis considers it distantly related to the Steneosaurus type species.

facts.statement: Andrews named the genus Mycterosuchus in 1913 based on fossils from the Oxford Clay of southern England.
facts.quote: The name Mycterosuchus was coined for Steneosaurus nasutus by Andrews in 1913 in his catalogue of thalattosuchians from the Oxford Clay of southern England.

facts.statement: The name Mycterosuchus means 'long-nosed crocodile', combining Latin and Greek roots.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Latin word for nose (mycto) and the Greek word for crocodile (), together meaning (long) nose crocodile.

facts.statement: Mycterosuchus nasutus was synonymized with Steneosaurus leedsi in 1987 but was recovered as a distinct species in a 2018 cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: Mycterosuchus nasutus fue sinonimizado con Steneosaurus leedsi por Adams-Tresmand en 1987, pero se recuperó como una especie distinta en el análisis cladístico de Osi et al. de 2018.

facts.statement: Mycterosuchus belongs to the family Teleosauridae.
Mycterosuchus lived during the Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Mycterosuchus is classified within the parent group Aeolodontini.
